NETWORK-LAYER flow statistics, which is a DIFFERENT TASK from the QKD-layer attack classifier on this same page: no shared labels and no shared features, so the two figures are not a comparison. 13 of the corpus's 52 columns are dropped before the model sees them, with reasons, in qsh.models.datasets.NIDD_DROPPED and in this model's feature_spec.json. Three of those are integer row identifiers whose restoration reproduces the accuracies published for this corpus; that counterfactual is the reason this model exists and is recorded in models/metrics.json as leak_counterfactual_*.

input.layout: samples[i] is one network flow's 39 features, in the order below. The five categorical columns are already ordinal-encoded against the published vocabulary in feature_spec.json; -1 means missing or out-of-vocabulary, for a categorical or a numeric alike

expected.note: NOT A PROPORTIONAL SAMPLE, so this macro F1 is not the 0.9264 the registry records on the full 303,973-row test split, and neither figure is wrong. Every class here is floored at 200 rows because a strictly proportional draw of this size gives ICMPFlood about 15, at which point its per-class F1 moves in steps of 1/15 and verifying against it would be theatre. The floor over-represents the four smallest classes, and since those are the classes the model is BEST at - seven of nine score above 0.98 while the two majority classes mutually confuse - it moves both figures upward. Read rows_per_class beside them. One further inversion, which is the opposite of this project's usual warning: on this corpus macro F1 is the optimistic number and accuracy the pessimistic one, because the two majority classes are 39.3% and 37.6% of the corpus and confuse with each other.
